exact_statement: For every even d>=2 and integer r>=1, let b be the canonical d-bit quadratic bent sign, Q_r the product of r independent two-bit signs negative only at 11, and F=b+1_(y=0)(Q_r-1). Put delta=2^-d,t=sqrt(delta),alpha=2^-r,w=4^(1-r),e=delta/2,A=1-delta+2delta alpha^2,R_sigma=1+2sigma t(alpha-1)+delta[(alpha-1)^2+alpha^2], and D_y=sum_sigma N_sigma delta log2(A/R_sigma). Every selector influence is e and every core influence is a=1/2+delta(1-alpha). Retaining only a queried selector bit partner gives binary laws (1/2,1/2),(1-e,e) and total influence-weighted binary loss at least r delta(3d/8-1/2) for r>=2; at r=2^d this loss cannot be paid by a fixed multiple of one specified core influence. Retaining also the empty/nonempty occupancy of all other selector pairs gives complete four-cell laws (w/2,(1-w)/2,w/2,(1-w)/2) and (A,e(1-w),ew,e(1-w)). Its per-row loss is e w D_y/2, with 0<=D_y<=log2(3)<2, and its retained price is M_i^C/e=1+(w/2)[d+2r-1+log2 A]. Summing over ALL selectors, their retained prices plus discarded losses above total selector influence J=r delta cost less than (3/2)a, charged once to y_1. Consequently the enlarged root audit bill 2I_core+sum_selector(M_i^C+L_i^C)+J/ln2 is <=(7/2)I(F), and dominates B(F). All spectral atoms are positive and H(F)<=4I(F). This is a complete root-row ownership fixture, not a universal signed partition, hereditary terminal-child reserve, or FEI theorem.
hypotheses: Actual Boolean signs on the uniform physical cube; entropy/KL in bits and ordinary influence
Even d>=2; r>=1 disjoint selector pairs and the specified bent core, edited only at its zero vertex
Complete row laws are marginalized, never conditioned on derivative support; zero cells omitted continuously
The single owner y_1 is allocated its baseline plus the combined selector extra once; no hereditary terminal-child surplus is inferred
refutes: All shared-core binary quotient losses for this family have a uniform payment by a fixed multiple of one core-coordinate influence

exact_statement: For every even integer d>=2, put delta=2^-d, t=2^(-d/2), b(y)=(-1)^(sum_j y_(2j-1)y_(2j)) on 0/1 labels, q(u,v)=-1 only at (1,1), and F_d=b(y)+1_(y=0)(q(u,v)-1). Every Fourier atom of F_d is positive. Each query i in {u,v} has e_i=delta/2 and positive true erasure. Retaining only the other pair coordinate gives complete derivative/reference laws (1/2,1/2) and (1-e_i,e_i). With N_+=(2^d+2^(d/2))/2,N_-=(2^d-2^(d/2))/2 and D0=sum_sigma N_sigma delta log2[(1-delta/2)/(1-sigma t+delta/2)], the full KL equals binary KL plus D0/2 and the influence-weighted quotient loss is L_i=e_i D0/2. Uniformly 0<L_i/e_i<=log2(7/5)/2<1/4-1/256, certified by 7^128<2^63*5^128. The two losses together are <delta/4 and <Inf_(y1)/10 if that physical reserve is dedicated only to these losses. Nevertheless M_i/e_i>d/2+3/4. Each core influence equals (1+delta)/2, I(F_d)=d/2+(d/2+1)delta, and H(F_d)/I(F_d)<=2+4/d<=4. No universal conditional partition, terminal payment, or FEI conclusion is asserted.
hypotheses: Actual uniform-cube Boolean signs; entropy and KL in bits; ordinary physical flip influence
Even d>=2, the specified quadratic bent core and two-bit gate on disjoint physical coordinates
Complete normalized reference laws including derivative-free mass; no reference conditioning on derivative support
Dedicated reserve inequality is only a partial ledger for the two stated quotient losses; no other charges or free global reserve are asserted
